title.narrative: Obligation to Protect and Empower Girls in Sudan (OPEG) 2022-2024
Obligation to Protect and Empower Girls in Sudan (OPEG) 2022-2024

description.narrative:
Overall goal/impact: Vulnerable children and youth in particular girls and young women live in communities free from all forms of violence, traditional harmful practices and gender discrimination, and are able to take decisions on their own lives.
Project purpose: Communities, civil society and government structures adopt positive social norms and laws to protect children's rights with a particular focus on tackling FGM and child marriage in Kassala, White Nile, and North Darfur.
The project included the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: Communities, women and men are empowered to bring about positive change to attitude and behaviours on gender equality.
Outcome 2: Civil society has strengthened capacity to promote gender equality, social accountability and advocacy to combat CEFM and FGM.
Outcome 3: Strengthened child protection systems, implementation of laws and policies to protect girls from CEFM and FGM/C.
Outcome 4: Strategic interventions to social norms transformation are identified.

Programmet implementeras under 2022-2024 i totalt 66 byar i Kassala, North Darfur och White Nile. Målet med OPEG-programmet är att minska nivån av kvinnlig könsstympning (FGM/c) och barn- och tvångsäktenskap (CEFM) men också att öka acceptansen och förståelsen i byarna kring jämställdhet och barns rättigheter. Detta sker genom att öka medvetenheten kring FGM/c och CEFM, gemensam identifiering av problem och lösningar i byarna, läs-och skrivkurser för kvinnor och ungdomar, stärka kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt genom att öka förutsättningarna för mikrolån och inkomstgenererande aktiviteter (IGA). Fokus läggs också på riktade insatser mot förändringsaktörer med inflytande i samhället såsom religiösa ledare och lärare, ungdomsklubbar för pojkar och flickor, påverkansarbete samt stärkande av de system som skyddar barn och unga kvinnor. En väsentlig del av programmet är att stärka civilsamhället för att påverka och driva förändring både på lokal och statlig nivå.

The program is implemented in a total of 66 villages in Kassala, North Darfur and White Nile. The objective of the OPEG program is to reduce the level of female genital mutilation (FGM/c) and child and forced marriage (CEFM) as well as increase acceptance and understanding in the communities regarding gender equality and children's rights. This is done by raising awareness around FGM/c and CEFM, community appraisal and planning, literacy classes for women and young people and strengthening women's financial empowerment by increasing the conditions for micro-loans and income-generating activities (IGA). The focus is also on targeted contributions against influential change actors such as religious leaders and teachers, youth clubs for boys and girls, advocacy and strengthening the systems that protect children and young women. An essential part of the program is strengthening civil society to influence and drive change at the local and state levels.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and Plan International Sverige regarding "Obligation to Protect and Empower Girls in Sudan (OPEG) 2022- 2024"
Decision on Contribution- Obligation to protect and empower girls in Sudan (OPEG) (15925) (7/12-22)

description.narrative:
The purpose of the Obligation to Protect and Empower Girls Phase 2 (OPEG2) programme was to ensure that communities, civil society, and government structures adopt positive social norms and laws to protect childrens rights, with particular focus on tackling Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting (FGM/C) and Child Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM). The selected locations for implementation were Kassala, North Darfur, and White Nile. These three states were selected due to high prevalence of FGM and CEFM, poverty and low access to education for girls.
Outcome 1: Communities women and men are empowered to bring about positive change to attitude and behaviours on gender equality.
Long-term outcomes include, but are not limited to, the following:
Very few baseline survey respondents were active in community measures to eliminate FGM/C and CEFM, and only 23% of parents and caregivers were active. However, at endline, 36% of parents and caregivers were active in OPEG 2 initiatives including community action plans, Saleema community meeting, REFLECT/VS&L groups, and CoC groups.
According to the final evaluation, 94% of children adolescents and youth (CAY) did not intend to have their daughter undergo FGM/C in the future. Prior to the OPEG programme, participants had little awareness of the harm FGM/C caused. However, during the endline evaluation, parents/caregivers and adolescents all referred to it as a source of psychological trauma, and significant physical harm. In addition, some participants perceived it as a form of post-marriage sexual violence (a significant shift away from the prior focus on male sexual pleasure) and framed it as a crime which should be punished.
At the baseline, 23% of parent/caregivers and 18% of CAY surveyed revealed that they would have their daughters go through FMG/C. Endline results demonstrated a significant change as only 6% of parents/caregivers, and 5% of CAY stated that they would subject their daughter to FGM/C.
25% of baseline survey respondents affirmed that FGM/C cannot be stopped. By the endline, this number had reduced significantly, especially among CAY. Among CAY, only 11% of respondents felt that FGM/C cannot be stopped, with 17% of parents/caregivers sharing this view.
Specific outputs included:
- 143 integrated REFLECT and village savings and loans associations (VSLA) groups (over the original target of 120) (68 groups, including 10 in IDP camp with 1 725 members in White Nile) and (75 groups with 1856 members in Kassala) were formed and empowered with financial and literacy skills and supported by 107 VSLA and REFLECT facilitators.
- 3 580 individuals (3 400 women and 180 men) including 15 persons with disabilities (14 women and one man) met on regular basis and discussed FGM/C and CEFM and gender equality issues in their communities. To address the psychosocial impact of the conflict on children and young people, Plan International and the Ministry of health (MOH) trained 107 teachers (51 women and 56 men in White Nile and Kassala) on psychosocial support, social norms and ending FGM/C and CEFM.
- CoC community facilitators were trained to roll out the comprehensive CoC methodology for the CoC groups formed. 3 060 members (girls and boys, including 31 living with disabilities (20 girls and 11 boys) completed the CoC curriculum.
Outcome 2: Civil society has strengthened capacity to promote gender equality, social accountability and advocacy to combat CEFM and FGM.
Long-term outcomes include, but are not limited to, the following:
Eight CSOs received support from Plan International to strategies, shape and implement advocacy plans. At the start of the programme, the implementing CSO partners with support from Plan International assessed their capacity needs and developed tailored development plans. The three implementing CSO partners received targeted capacity development support and showed signs of improvement in several areas, especially CRCS and FPDO. The final evaluation report stated that OPEG 2 actively engaged with CSOs and Community-Based Organisations (CBOs) to enhance their capacity to promote gender equality and prevent FGM/C and CEFM. CSOs which participated in the programme evaluation were very satisfied with the training and support they received from OPEG 2. They perceived it as useful in developing gender sensitive approaches and advocating against FGM/C and CEFM.
Specific outputs included:
-30 CSO/CBO member organisations (14 in Kassala and 16 in White Nile) including youth and women led organisations were trained on gender equality, social norma (including FGM/C, CEFM, SRHR), and advocacy.
-15 CSO/CBOs (6 in White Nile, including CRCS and 9 in Kassala, including FPDO) took part in CSO alliance meetings to develop and submitted advocacy plans focusing on empowering girls, gender equality, and social transformation.
-Eight advocacy plans (4 in West Nile and 4 in Kassala) were implemented by CSOs/CBOs/ after they attended a safeguarding training.
Outcome 3: Strengthened child protection systems, implementation of laws and policies to protect girls from CEFM and FGM/C.
Long-term outcomes include, but are not limited to, the following:
The CBCPMs conducted 224 monthly meetings, and helped raise awareness in their communities on SGBV, FGM/C and CEFM prevention and conducted 206 awareness raising sessions reaching a total of 18,335 community members (7 134 women, 5 867 men, 2 957 girls, and 2 377 boys) including 201 persons with disabilities (71 women, 64 men, 24 girls and 41 boys).
The final evaluation report highlighted that the baseline data indicated a low awareness among children and adults of government agencies and child protection mechanisms. At the endline, 46% of CAY reported awareness of child protection systems, laws, and policies safeguarding girls from FGM/C and CEFM (58% in Kassala; 38% in White Nile)
Specific outputs included:
-Plan International established, trained, and supported 32 community CVCPMs with a total of 537 members (consisting of, as per the guidelines of the government, community leaders, women, men, children (299 women and 238 men), including 13 persons with disabilities (5 women, 3 men, 3 girls and 2 boys). The trainings covered child rights child protection risks and how to deal with children and responding to childs issue including referral pathways/mechanisms.
-To contribute to strengthening the child protection systems, to promote gender equality and the prevention of child marriage and FGM/C, a workshop was conducted on case management and information management for the child protection sub-sector, targeting 20 women and 10 men. This workshop discussed how to handle FGM/C and child marriage cases and child protection concerns.
Outcome 4: Strategic interventions to social norms transformation are identified.
Long-term outcomes include, but are not limited to, the following:
The final evaluation confirmed positive shifts in social norms: fewer respondents agreed that FGM/C was a prerequisite for marriage (-18% combined reduction) and fewer community members approved of the practice (-21% combined reduction). There was also less of discriminatory attitudes against girls and women who had not undergone FGM/C and a decline in negative attitudes towards families with unmarried daughters (-15.5% combined reduction). These findings highlighted the effectiveness of Saleema in reinforcing gender-transformative change and breaking down entrenched norms, despite the complex context and gradual nature of social transformation. Also, CoCs were greatly valued by both adolescents and adults. Adults observed that such youth outreach was extremely successful in fostering a gender transformative change at the community level.
Specific outputs included:
- The final evaluation confirmed positive shifts in social norms: fewer respondents agreed that FGM/C was a prerequisite for marriage (-18% combined reduction) and fewer community members approved of the practice (-21% combined reduction).
- 122 (49 women and 73 men) religious and community leaders, women leaders and youth were trained on Article 141, the code of conduct to end FGM/C legislation and support ending CEFM policies. 52 participants (29 women and 23 men), including media activists, radio journalists, officials from the Ministry of Media, champions of change facilitators and artists were trained on advocacy to end CEFM and FGM/C.
- Plan International produced and broadcasted 13 radio programmes each for White Nile state and Kassala state, reaching an estimated audience of 881 674 in Kassala state and 1.1 million in While Nile. In North Darfur, only five radio programmes were produced and aired before broadcasts were interrupted due to the deteriorating security situation, reaching an estimated audience of 980,000.
- In 22 communities (7 in White Nile and 15 in Kassala) code of conduct for traditional midwives was developed and monitored by the CBCPMs.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
